text:
Rae: FYI onboarding hit a snag: sampleapp tries to register a webhook via the SDK but gets 401 when using ephemeral tokens; same curl with same token works.
Tom: oof. paste both?
Rae: curl that succeeds:
```
curl -X POST \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL_TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/webhooks \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/hook","events":["deployment.created"]}'
```
Rae: SDK call (failing):
```js
await client.admin.createWebhook({ url: 'https://example.com/hook', events: ['deployment.created'] })
// Error: 401 Unauthorized: token expired or invalid
```
Anika: Does the SDK refresh tokens under the hood? Ephemeral tokens should be passed through unchanged.
Tom: SDK has an auth middleware that adds `Authorization` header from credentials provider. For ephemeral token flows we changed the provider to rotate tokens automatically and it was normalizing header casing + adding a cache TTL. Could be the header being overwritten or the token being base64-wrapped accidentally.
Rae: I captured the outgoing request: SDK sent header `authorization: Bearer \"$EPHEMERAL_TOKEN\"` (quotes included) — backend rejects it. The curl sends header without quotes.
Anika: ah, quotes slipped in during our new string-escaping change in 2.0.5 when handling JS env vars. The token provider was calling `JSON.stringify(token)` for safety and not stripping quotes.
Jules: That explains 401. But why only for webhooks? Other routes with ephemeral tokens worked for sampleapp earlier.
Tom: Webhooks route is proxied through the gateway which has stricter auth parsing and refuses quoted tokens; some other endpoints did tolerant parsing. The gateway change to strict auth was deployed last week.
Rae: Workaround for onboarding: use raw request and pass header manually: `client.request('POST','/v1/admin/webhooks', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer '+token } })` — that avoids provider formatting. Verified it succeeds.
sdk-bot: Created issue #3801: "js-sdk: auth provider JSON.stringify token adds quotes leading to 401 on strict-auth endpoints". Linking sampleapp logs.
Anika: I'll push a patch to stop stringifying tokens and add a unit test that asserts header is exact bytes with no extra quotes.
Tom: Also add an integration test against gateway that exercises strict endpoints (webhooks, billing) to catch tolerant-vs-strict differences.
ops-bot: deploy: PR #834 merged to sdk-auth; hotfix release 2.0.6 queued.
Jules: Two follow-ups: (1) audit other credential providers for similar stringification (env vars, k8s secrets), (2) add a short note in devex onboarding doc that ephemeral token flows need raw header passthrough until SDK patch lands.
Rae: Thanks all — using manual header for now, will retry onboarding when 2.0.6 hits. :thumbsup:
